- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day window; reduce forecasts by 1–2% for the first 5–7 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model tends to overshoot and stay high; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use moving average of last 5 days.
- Model underestimates prices during low-volatility periods (e.g., 70–72 range); add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if 3 consecutive days are below 72.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day window; if forecast is >75 for 3+ days, reduce by 1–2% per day until it aligns with 70–74 range.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum after spikes; if true outcome drops >1.5% from peak, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for next 3 days.
- Forecast bias is stronger in early 2025 (June 19–24) — apply 1.5–2.0% downward adjustment for forecasts made before June 25.
